union.summary:
`isLoneDash` rejects every single-dash setext underline, including valid top-level `Title\n-` headings, which now render as a paragraph plus a spurious empty `
`
union.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` (line 105) followed by `if (pos >= max && !isLoneDash)` (line 107) is unconditional — it does not check that the paragraph being underlined is a list-item paragraph, nor that a list context exists. For plain prose `Title\n-`, lheading now returns false, and then the wrapped `list` rule (line ~182) reports the lone `-` as a paragraph terminator because `state.parentType === 'paragraph'` and `isEmptyBulletLine` is true, so the non-silent `list` rule builds a real list on that line. Result: `

Title

` instead of `

Title

` — the heading is lost and a bullet the author never intended is injected. `docs/design/notes/notes.md` (added block) asserts "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched, so ordinary setext headings still render", which is false for the equally ordinary single-dash `-` underline; the todo file even lists a "top-level lone dash" test case that was not added, so nothing pins this behavior.

union.summary: The paragraph-interrupt relaxation also fires for `*` and `+` empty bullets, changing rendering for input that the #517 bug never affected (including swallowing a lone `*`/`+` line out of prose and out of setext heading content)
union.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `0x2a /* * */` and `0x2b /* + */` (line 39), and `wrappedList` uses it to short-circuit `return true` in silent mode (line ~182-190). `lheading` never claimed `*`/`+` lines, so these shapes were not part of the bug, yet: (a) `1 *` previously rendered as one paragraph containing the literal `*` and now renders `

1

`, dropping the typed marker from the output; (b) upstream `1 * ===` renders `

` with `1 *` as content, because stock `list` refuses to interrupt with an empty bullet and the scan continues to the `===` underline — with the wrapper, the very first terminator call on the `*` line returns true, so both `lheading` and `paragraph` stop there and the h1 is lost. The design note and todo scope the deviation to "a lone single `-`"; the implementation is broader than what is documented or tested.

union.summary:
`isLoneDash` (lheading) and `isEmptyBulletLine` (list wrapper) disagree on which trailing whitespace counts, so a dash followed by `\v`/`\f` gets neither a heading nor a bullet — it degrades to exactly the lazy `1
-` text the change set out to avoid
union.evidence: In `lheadingRule` the underline test uses `state.skipSpaces(pos)` (line 100), and markdown-it's `isSpace` treats 0x0b/0x0c as space, so `-\x0b` yields `isLoneDash === true` and lheading declines. But `isEmptyBulletLine` gates on `isSpaceOrTab` (line 45, only 0x20/0x09), so it returns false for the same line; `wrappedList` then delegates to the stock `list`, whose `isTerminatingParagraph` empty-item check rejects it. No terminator fires, the paragraph absorbs the line, and the output is the lazy `1\n-` text the plugin's own doc comment calls the bad outcome. The two predicates should use the same whitespace class.

union.summary: `getRuleFn` reads the private `__rules__` registry and throws during module initialization, so a markdown-it internal rename would break the entire notes preview module import rather than just losing the fix
union.evidence: `ruler.__rules__.find(...)` with `if (!rule) throw new Error(...)` (lines ~205-210) is executed from `listEmptyBulletPlugin`, which `preview.ts` invokes at module top level (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)`). A throw there is not caught anywhere, so the ES-module evaluation of `preview.ts` fails and every consumer of the preview dies at import time (blank preview / broken notes view) instead of degrading to the pre-fix rendering. It also ignores the entry's `enabled` flag, and it snapshots `list`'s fn at plugin-install time, so it silently loses the wrapper if any later-installed plugin calls `ruler.at('list', ...)`.

union.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` may not match the trimming the upstream `lheading` rule actually performs, changing setext heading content for unusual whitespace
union.evidence: Lines 19-23 define `ASCII_TRIM_RE` and `asciiTrim`, used at line ~134 for the heading content, on the stated premise that markdown-it uses an `asciiTrim`. markdown-it's `lheading` computes `state.getLines(...).trim()`, and JS `String.prototype.trim()` also strips Unicode whitespace (NBSP U+00A0, U+2028, BOM, ...). Where a heading line ends in such a character, this replacement leaves it in the heading text while stock markdown-it strips it. I could not verify against the installed markdown-it: the reviewed package and its node_modules are not present in the materialized tree (only `agent/` exists), hence low confidence.

union.summary: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)` replaces the rule wholesale, so any lheading customization installed by an earlier plugin (e.g. `detailsPlugin`, applied on the preceding line) is silently discarded
union.evidence: `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` runs after `md.use(detailsPlugin)` in preview.ts, and the plugin calls `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` (plugin line ~176), which overwrites the rule fn and resets its `alt` chain to `[]` rather than composing with whatever is registered. Unlike the `list` case, no delegation to the previous fn happens, so a prior lheading override would be lost with no error. I could not inspect `details-plugin.ts` to confirm whether it touches `lheading` — the notes package is not present in the materialized working tree — hence low confidence.

union.summary: Empty-bullet paragraph interrupt fires at top level too, silently destroying single-dash setext H2s and injecting a phantom empty list
union.evidence:
`wrappedList` returns `true` (terminate paragraph) for ANY line matching `isEmptyBulletLine` whenever `state.parentType === 'paragraph'` — there is no requirement that the paragraph be inside a list item. Combined with `lheadingRule`'s `isLoneDash` guard (line 106), the perfectly ordinary top-level document Title - no longer renders `

Title

`: `lheading` declines the lone dash, the wrapper terminates the paragraph, and the non-silent `list` rule then builds a spurious empty list, giving `

Title

`. The design note only promises that `---` and `=` underlines are untouched, and the desired behavior in the todo is about *nested* empty bullets; a lone `-` underline (valid CommonMark H2, widely used) is now unrenderable anywhere in a note, and the output gains an empty bullet the author never wrote. Neither the todo's planned 'top-level lone dash' test nor any test in the diff covers this shape, so the regression is unguarded.

union.summary: The paragraph-interrupt relaxation also applies to `*` and `+` markers, which have no setext ambiguity, changing rendering of lone-asterisk lines
union.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `-`, `*` and `+` (line 40: `marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a && marker !== 0x2b`), and `wrappedList` uses it to terminate paragraphs. Only `-` participates in the setext ambiguity the change is about (the `lheading` replacement is deliberately restricted to DASH via `isLoneDash`). Consequence: `some text\n*` and `some text\n+`, which upstream/CommonMark render as literal text inside the paragraph, now render as `

some text

`. That is broader than what both the design note (`a lone single -`) and the plugin's own doc comment claim, and it is untested.

union.summary: `asciiTrim` under-trims compared to upstream `.trim()`, leaking non-ASCII whitespace into setext heading text
union.evidence: Upstream markdown-it 14 `lheading` computes `state.getLines(...).trim()`; this copy substitutes `asciiTrim` (lines 20-24), which only strips \x09-\x0d and \x20. `String.prototype.trim()` also strips NBSP (U+00A0), U+2000-200A, U+3000, U+2028/2029 and U+FEFF. So `Heading \n---` now yields heading content with a trailing NBSP where stock markdown-it produced clean text — a silent behavioral divergence in a rule this change only meant to add one dash-length guard to. The comment claiming markdown-it has its own `asciiTrim` for this rule appears to be incorrect for `lheading`.

union.summary: Private `__rules__` access can throw a TypeError at module import time, and `originalList` is captured at install time so later `list` replacements are silently bypassed
union.evidence: `getRuleFn` does `(md.block.ruler as ...).__rules__.find(...)`. If markdown-it ever renames or hides `__rules__`, `__rules__` is `undefined` and `.find` throws a TypeError — not the friendly `Error(...)` on the next line. This runs during `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at the top level of `preview.ts`, so the failure is a module-evaluation crash that takes down the whole notes preview module rather than degrading one render. Separately, `originalList` is a snapshot of the rule function at install time: any plugin registered after `listEmptyBulletPlugin` that replaces `list` via `ruler.at('list', ...)` would be silently bypassed for every non-empty-bullet line (the wrapper delegates to the stale original), and hardcoding `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` likewise discards any `alt` extension an earlier plugin made.

union.summary: `isEmptyBulletLine` omits the upstream `list` rule's indent bounds, so the wrapper can answer 'this terminates the paragraph' for a line the real `list` rule then refuses
union.evidence: Upstream `list` rejects a line early when `state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (indented code) and in the `listIndent` paragraph-continuation special case. `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks the lower bound (`state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent`), and `wrappedList` returns `true` without consulting those bounds. For e.g. `- 1\n      -` (6 spaces, blkIndent 2) the wrapper would report termination while the non-silent `list` rule returns false, so the line would be picked up by the `code` rule and the lazy paragraph continuation would turn into an indented code block. Today this is latent because the only rules that set `parentType='paragraph'` (`paragraph`, and the new `lheadingRule` at line 87) skip terminator checks for lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3`; it becomes a live rendering bug for any other rule/plugin (e.g. the sibling `details-plugin`) that consults `getRules('paragraph')` in paragraph mode without that guard. I could not open the working tree to check `details-plugin.ts`, hence low confidence.
